aAttempts: From 'stamp each cached mark with GOOGLEFINANCE's quote date, not wall-clock read time' alone: build Mark{price,quote_date}; read price+a paired quote-date signal per symbol each settle poll; write quote_date verbatim into the mark. Invented assumptions: (1) a per-symbol quote-date value is always available whenever price is, no partial/missing case; (2) mechanism for reading it is unspecified (formula cell vs direct API field); (3) nothing said about retry/carry-forward on a bad reading.

Naive misreading as purely negative ('don't use wall clock') — dev could pick ANY non-wall-clock per-symbol date proxy (e.g. reuse an existing lot/trade date already in the system) rather than actually fetching GOOGLEFINANCE's own trade date, since the spec doesn't name the retrieval mechanism at all.

Strict-coupling naive design: treat quote-date failure as coupling to price failure — if the date can't be determined, treat the WHOLE poll as still-transient (retry within the settle window) rather than accepting a numeric price with a degraded/fallback date. This is a plausible, even stricter, naive reading that the real code does NOT follow (real code accepts the numeric price and just backfills the date).
